title: Encoding with the same settings leads to differences in file, maybe even privacy problem
body:
### Problem Description

When encoding a video with the same settings twice in a row, there are slightly differences in the file. For comparing see for example https://superuser.com/a/125408

There might be some encodingtimestamps or other stuff included which from my point of view shouldn't be the case. Encoding with the same settings should lead to exactly the same file.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: Are you referring to the differences in the encoded comments, which list when a file was encoded? There will be differences in those comments, which are always included in the file.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
All comments are empty for the checked file
![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37013344/176443911-2f01b3b5-98f0-4c03-ac95-b26b0c7d7a5b.png)

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
This is not actually always the case. Encoders can be non-deterministic (by design. It's not a bug). 
As such, for the same input and settings, you may get a different output.  You won't be able to tell by watching the video as the difference is not typically perceptible. 

Metadata such Encoded Date, Tagged Date etc will also affect the file hash. (This is visible in MediaInfo. I don't think VLC shows these fields)

Regardless, this is expected and nothing to worry about.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
Thank you very much. mediainfo shows all the information. Both encodings differ in
`Encoded date` and `Unique ID`

Is it possible to omit both fields when encoding with handbrake? Giving information when a file was encoded can be sensitive information in some case.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body: Nope.  You'd have to strip it out after the fact with a meta data editor tool.
